derived.reason: AWS resources are drawn inside the AWS Cloud frame.
AWS resources that belong to a Region are drawn inside that Region's frame.
No Region was given, so ap-northeast-1 (Tokyo) is used.
An Application Load Balancer is created in subnets of a VPC, so a VPC is drawn.
An Application Load Balancer requires subnets in at least two Availability Zones.
No number of Availability Zones was given, so two are used, the minimum an Application Load Balancer accepts.
archwire gives each Availability Zone one public subnet and one private subnet.

AWS lists Amazon CloudFront and AWS WAF for CloudFront among the global services, whose resources are not Region-specific. archwire draws global services inside the AWS Cloud frame and outside the Region frame.
No subnet was given, so ECS is placed in private subnets; traffic reaches it through the load balancer.
No subnet was given, so Aurora is placed in private subnets so it is not reachable from the internet.
The Writer goes in the first Availability Zone and Readers in the remaining ones.
Regional services that are not placed in a VPC subnet are drawn inside the Region frame and outside the VPC frame.
Regional services that are not placed in a VPC subnet are drawn inside the Region frame and outside the VPC frame.

To use an AWS Certificate Manager certificate with a CloudFront distribution, the certificate is requested or imported in US East (N. Virginia) (us-east-1). archwire draws it outside the Region frame and writes us-east-1 under its name.

Certificates in AWS Certificate Manager are regional resources: to use a certificate with Elastic Load Balancing for the same domain names in more than one Region, a certificate is requested or imported for each Region, and a certificate cannot be copied between Regions. archwire draws the certificate attached to an Application Load Balancer inside the Region frame.

A web ACL (protection pack) and the AWS WAF resources it uses must be located in the same Region as the resources it protects, and an Application Load Balancer is one of the regional resource types AWS WAF can protect. archwire draws the web ACL attached to an Application Load Balancer inside the Region frame.
With an internet-facing Application Load Balancer, only VPCs that have an Internet Gateway can be selected, so the VPC gets an Internet Gateway.
Resources in a private subnet can connect to the internet through a NAT device in a public subnet, which replaces their source IPv4 addresses with its own.

You can use the managed NAT device AWS offers, the NAT gateway, or build your own NAT device on EC2, a NAT instance; AWS recommends NAT gateways for better availability and bandwidth and less administration. archwire draws a NAT gateway.
Resources in a private subnet can connect to the internet through a NAT device in a public subnet, which replaces their source IPv4 addresses with its own.

You can use the managed NAT device AWS offers, the NAT gateway, or build your own NAT device on EC2, a NAT instance; AWS recommends NAT gateways for better availability and bandwidth and less administration. archwire draws a NAT gateway.
One NAT gateway per Availability Zone keeps outbound traffic working when another zone fails.

notes: Auxiliary flows (~>) are drawn as lines only; their network route is not handled.
